{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the bottom body line of the fish, which is the longest single stretch of the outline and connects into the run from the start. I also laid the straight back edge of the tail and several joins at the tail junction. I re-laid and carried on the top body line from the pad so it flows out of the junction. I spent most of my dominoes on the busiest, most crowded part of the table, where the body, tail and start line all meet. The fish outline, with its body, tail fin and nose, is all standing.

Execution: I took my stroke assignment at the start and had it down within the first couple of minutes. After that I kept inspecting the junction closely to find where the fall was stopping. I tried several joins and bridges from the dark line toward the pale top line, and I used my full domino allowance on that corner. I stopped placing when we ran out and left the table untouched before the push.

Collaboration: I told the table what I was working on and which area I needed clear, and I thanked people for staying off it. I split work with Leo and Tom, handing off the nose check and the back edge. I accepted Priya's and Leo's help on the nose and the final join. I also gave the manager straight status updates every time they checked in.

Leadership: I set the pace by committing to the fish idea immediately and taking a big stroke. I called out time pressure and asked teammates for specific checks along the run. At the end I called hands-off so nobody disturbed the build before the push. I took ownership of the hardest corner of the build and kept the table informed about it throughout.", "my_share_percent": 35}
